text:
Erin: Heads-up — noticed a host-side CPU jump after yesterday's runtime kernel rollout. 3.8ms extra p99 add-on on short text workloads. :eyes:
Sam: saw that too. spikes around request parse + tokenization + grpc writev batching.
Kevin: any correlation with kernel selection? last rollout changed kernel_picker heuristics, right?
Erin: yes, kernel_picker started preferring the quant-int8 path for many shards. perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood/ingress/4789 (iamg link)
Maria: hmm int8 is cheaper per-token but for small batches it looks worse due to extra prep and slower memcpy paths. KV cache interactions might amplify that.
Sam: short run from flamegraph on a 128-char request:
```
flamegraph --service=hostparse --span=ingress --last=1h
Top stacks:
  host_tokenize (45%)
  grpc_writev (18%)
  parse_proto (12%)
  kernel_select (8%)
  kv_cache_get (7%)
```
Kevin: interesting that kernel_select is only 8% but host_tokenize dominates. maybe tokenization glue got a regression in the proxy that increased syscall churn.
Erin: timeline: PR #1221 changed chunking window + writev coalesce and PR #1239 changed kernel hint thresholds. both landed yesterday.
Zach: infra-bot started a canary last night and auto-rolled after success. infra-bot: deploy canary 2026-03-22T23:40 UTC -> rolled 2026-03-23T02:10 UTC :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: Canary metrics: host_cpu +9%, p99 latency +3.8ms, kv_cache_hit -17% on small requests.
Maria: kv_cache_hit down 17% is huge. maybe the new chunk splice changed request keys or prefixing so cache miss rate increases.
Sam: reproduced locally with stress harness. If I force kernel_picker to prefer the legacy fp16 path, host cpu drops back and p99 improves. Quick test patch:
```
# revert kernel hint in staging
diff --git a/kernel/picker.cc b/kernel/picker.cc
- prefer_int8_for_small_shards = true
+ prefer_int8_for_small_shards = false
```
Erin: can we run an A/B? small sample in prod preferring fp16 for <16 tokens. Zach — can you coordinate canary?
Zach: yup. spinning up a 5% canary. will route only short-text traffic.
Kevin: also want to check tokenization path — the new proto splice changed framing and we saw extra allocations. cheap fix might be to reuse the parse buffer across requests (pool).
Maria: I dug into the proto splice changes — we added a tiny header transform for streaming chunk reassembly that does an extra memcpy per frame. That plus writev fragmentation causes syscall pressure.
Sam: numbers from microbench: additional memcpy ~120ns per frame, but with many small frames it sums to ~2.5ms per request.
Erin: proposal: revert kernel hint change in prod, add a short-term token buffer pool, and instrument KV keys to ensure chunking doesn't change cache keys.
Maria: I'll open two PRs: 1) buffer pool (low-risk); 2) KV key guard (audit + test).
Sam: i'll prepare a revert PR for kernel picker and a perf test matrix to validate small-batch behavior (int8 vs fp16 vs fp32).
Zach: canary is up (5%). initial metrics: p99 down 2.9ms vs baseline with rollback candidate, host CPU trending down. will hold for 30m and then decide.
Kevin: long-term we should adapt kernel_picker to prefer paths by batch-size *and* kv_cache_hit probability, not just shard size. works better for PLG workloads.
Erin: agreed. add to roadmap: kernel-picker adaptive heuristic (batch-size + kv-hit + recent-latency). prioritize quick revert + buffer pool first.
Sam: FYI, reproduced a synthetic that mimics the customer's short prompt burst and saw same KV miss pattern — I can paste harness config if helpful.
Maria: please do. also add a sentinel in telemetry to log chunking prefix so we can compare keys pre/post-change without PII.
Erin: action items:
- Maria: open buffer-pool PR + KV key audit (#A)
- Sam: revert kernel hint PR + perf matrix (#B)
- Zach: monitor canary + hold rollback window (#C)
- Kevin: spec adaptive kernel_picker heuristic for follow-up (#D)
Erin: thanks everyone. keep thread brief updates here. if canary degrades more I'll call for immediate rollback. :pray:
